cases.summary: Federal credit in the financial model does not match the QRE
cases.claims_compared: DOC-05 shows a federal credit of $5,120,000. DOC-05 and DOC-06 both show QRE of $24,600,000, and DOC-06 gives the credit as $4,920,000.

citations.raw: DOC-05 p.2, 2.1: "24,600 ($ in thousands)"

cases.explanation: The federal credit is 20% of QRE. $24.6M x 20% = $4.92M, so the model overstates the credit by $200,000, and the investor equity built on it.

cases.summary: Budget counts non-qualifying costs as QRE
cases.claims_compared: DOC-04 totals qualified costs at $25,310,000, including a $420,000 parking lot and $290,000 of furniture. DOC-06 certifies QRE of $24,600,000.

citations.raw: DOC-04 p.2, line 38: "Total qualified costs $25,310,000"

cases.explanation: Parking lots and furniture do not qualify. Taking out $710,000 brings the budget to $24,600,000, which matches the cost certification. Any credit worked out from the budget figure is overstated.

cases.summary: Cost certification leaves out the change orders
cases.claims_compared: DOC-08 shows three change orders totaling $640,000, bringing the contract to $22,540,000. DOC-06 certifies a construction contract of $21,900,000 with no change orders.

citations.raw: DOC-08 p.9, change order log: "$22,540,000"
DOC-06 p.2, 3: "Construction contract $21,900,000"

cases.explanation: The cost certification uses the original contract sum. The change orders are either missing from certified costs or left out without explanation, so certified costs may be understated.
cases.open_questions: Were any of the change orders for non-qualifying work?

cases.summary: Financial model and summaries use the draft credit price, not the signed one
cases.claims_compared: DOC-12, the signed agreement, sets the Virginia credit price at $0.82. DOC-05, DOC-15 and DOC-16 use $0.85, the price in the unsigned draft DOC-13.

citations.raw: DOC-12 p.3, Section 2.1: "$0.82 per $1.00 of credit"
DOC-05 p.2, 2.7: "5,227.5 ($ in thousands)"
DOC-15 p.6, email Mar 4, 2025: "pricing came in at 85 cents"
DOC-16 p.1, 3: "$0.85 per credit"

cases.explanation: The signed agreement governs. At $0.82, proceeds are $5,043,000, not $5,227,500, a shortfall of $184,500. The same wrong price appears in three documents and should be reported once.

cases.summary: Signed and draft purchase agreements give different prices
cases.claims_compared: DOC-12, signed, sets the price at $0.82. DOC-13, an unsigned later draft, shows $0.85.

citations.raw: DOC-12 p.3, Section 2.1: "$0.82 per $1.00 of credit"
DOC-13 p.3, Section 2.1: "$0.85 per $1.00 of credit"

cases.explanation: The draft was never signed, so the signed price stands. Two versions of an agreement differing is expected and is not a discrepancy on its own. The real issue is HTC01-004, where other documents rely on the draft.
cases.alternative_readings: A reviewer could note that a price change was attempted. That is context, not a conflict.

cases.summary: Memo says the project is fully funded, but the budget shows a gap
cases.claims_compared: DOC-16 says the project is fully funded. DOC-04 shows sources of $31,150,000 against uses of $31,750,000, a $600,000 gap.

citations.raw: DOC-16 p.1, 2: "The project is fully funded"
DOC-04 p.1, line 24: "Total uses $31,750,000"

cases.explanation: The budget itself shows a $600,000 shortfall. An investor reading the memo would not know the gap exists.
cases.open_questions: Has the gap been closed since the budget date?

cases.summary: Memo puts the federal credits in the wrong tax year
cases.claims_compared: DOC-16 says federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return. DOC-06 gives the placed-in-service date as July 15, 2025.

citations.quote: Federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return
citations.raw: DOC-16 p.2, 5: "Federal credits will be claimed on the 2024 return"

cases.explanation: Credits for a building placed in service after 2017 are claimed in five equal parts, starting with the year it is placed in service. A July 15, 2025 date means the first 20% goes on the 2025 return and the last on the 2029 return. Nothing can be claimed on a 2024 return.

cases.summary: Two different construction start dates, one before Part 2 approval
cases.claims_compared: DOC-08 has a notice to proceed dated June 5, 2023. DOC-09 shows construction starting October 2, 2023. DOC-02 shows Part 2 approved on August 22, 2023.

citations.raw: DOC-08 p.1, 1: "Notice to Proceed dated June 5, 2023"
DOC-02 p.1, approval letter: "August 22, 2023"

cases.explanation: If work began in June, it started before NPS approved the scope, which puts certification at risk. The documents disagree on the start date, so it has to be confirmed.
cases.alternative_readings: The June date may be when the notice was issued, with work on site starting in October. On the face of the documents it is still a conflict.
cases.open_questions: When did work on site actually begin?

cases.summary: Part 3 approval is claimed but not in the data room
cases.claims_compared: DOC-15 says NPS approved Part 3 in October. No Part 3 approval is in the data room. DOC-11 ties the 40% equity installment to Part 3 approval.

citations.raw: DOC-15 p.11, email Nov 3, 2025: "NPS approved Part 3 in October"
DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(c): "40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval"

cases.explanation: Part 3 approval cannot be confirmed from the documents. Until it is, the third installment of $1,731,840 should not be treated as due.

cases.summary: No evidence NPS approved the window shop drawings before installation
cases.claims_compared: DOC-02 requires NPS approval of window shop drawings before installation. DOC-15 reports windows installed on floors 1 to 3 in September 2024. Nothing in the data room shows the drawings were approved.

citations.quote: Shop drawings for replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS before installation
citations.raw: DOC-02 p.3, condition 2: "Shop drawings for replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS before installation"
DOC-15 p.4, update Sep 2024: "Windows installed on floors 1 to 3"

cases.explanation: If the condition was not met, Part 3 certification could be at risk. The NPS response is needed before this can be closed.
cases.open_questions: Did NPS respond to the shop drawings?

cases.summary: Window quote is for vinyl, but the approval requires wood
cases.claims_compared: DOC-02 requires replacement windows to replicate the original wood profiles, and DOC-07 specifies wood. DOC-14, the supplier quote, is for vinyl double-hung windows with a standard profile.

citations.quote: Shop drawings for replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS before installation
citations.raw: DOC-02 p.3, condition 2: "Shop drawings for replacement windows must be submitted to and approved by NPS before installation"
DOC-07 p.6, Section 08 52 00: "Wood windows replicating original profiles"
DOC-14 p.1, item 1: "Vinyl double-hung, standard profile"

cases.explanation: Vinyl windows would not meet the Part 2 condition, which could cost the project its certification. Which windows were actually ordered and installed must be confirmed.
cases.open_questions: Was the vinyl quote replaced by a wood window order?

cases.summary: Appraisal and architect disagree on the unit count

citations.raw: DOC-07 p.1, 1: "84 apartments"
DOC-10 p.2, 1: "86 units"

cases.explanation: No phase, commercial space or date explains the difference. Unit count drives rent and the appraised value.

cases.summary: Gross area and rentable area differ

citations.raw: DOC-10 p.2, 2: "112,400 SF gross building area"
DOC-07 p.1, 2: "78,650 rentable SF"

cases.explanation: Gross area includes corridors, walls and common space, and rentable area does not. Both figures are correct.

cases.summary: Equity installments do not add up to the equity amount
cases.claims_compared: DOC-11 sets federal investor equity at $4,329,600, but its four installments add up to $4,429,600. Installment 3 reads $1,831,840, while 40% of equity is $1,731,840.
cases.explanation: Installment 3 is overstated by $100,000. The pay-in schedule has to match total equity.

cases.summary: Developer fee in the budget is above the operating agreement cap
cases.claims_compared: DOC-04 shows a developer fee of $2,750,000. DOC-11 caps the fee at $2,500,000.

citations.raw: DOC-11 p.18, Section 6.3: "shall not exceed $2,500,000"

cases.explanation: The budget fee is $250,000 over the cap. Either the budget is wrong or the fee breaches the agreement.

cases.summary: Operating agreement gives two different guaranty caps
cases.claims_compared: DOC-11 Section 7.4 caps the recapture guaranty at $1,500,000. Exhibit C of the same agreement caps it at $1,000,000.

citations.raw: DOC-11 p.42, Exhibit C, paragraph 2: "$1,000,000"

cases.explanation: The investor's protection depends on which figure governs, and the agreement contradicts itself.
cases.open_questions: Which provision does the agreement say controls?

cases.summary: Cost certification names the developer as taxpayer, not the building owner
cases.claims_compared: DOC-06 names Riverside Heritage Development LLC as the taxpayer. DOC-10 shows Ashby Mill Owner LLC as the owner of the building.

citations.raw: DOC-06 p.1, 1: "Taxpayer: Riverside Heritage Development LLC"

citations.quote: Ashby Mill Owner LLC, fee simple owner
citations.raw: DOC-10 p.1, 3: "Ashby Mill Owner LLC, fee simple owner"

cases.explanation: Only the building's owner can claim the credit. If the certification names the wrong entity, the credit claim and the investor's admission are at risk.

citations.raw: DOC-07 p.1, title block: "Ashbey Mill Owner LLC"
DOC-11 p.1, preamble: "Ashby Mill Owner LLC"

cases.explanation: A typo with no money or eligibility impact, but it should be corrected.

citations.raw: DOC-12 p.1, preamble: "Ashby Mill Owner, L.L.C."
DOC-11 p.1, preamble: "Ashby Mill Owner LLC"

citations.quote: approximately $24.6 million of qualified rehabilitation expenses
citations.raw: DOC-16 p.1, 4: "approximately $24.6 million of qualified rehabilitation expenses"
DOC-16 p.1, 4: "$4.9M in federal credits"

cases.explanation: $4.92M rounds to $4.9M at the memo's precision. Rounding is not a discrepancy.

citations.raw: DOC-02 p.1, approval letter: "August 22, 2023"

citations.raw: DOC-03 p.8, 4: "7 units per month; stabilization in about 12 months"

citations.raw: DOC-16 p.2, 6: "Virginia DHR has issued final certification for the state credits"

cases.summary: Update treats the Phase 1 temporary occupancy date as the placed-in-service date
cases.claims_compared: DOC-15 says the building was placed in service on March 28, 2025, with the Phase 1 temporary certificate. DOC-06 and DOC-09 give July 15, 2025.

citations.quote: Building placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO
citations.raw: DOC-15 p.8, update Apr 2025: "Building placed in service March 28 with the Phase 1 TCO"

cases.explanation: A temporary certificate for floors 1 to 3 does not place the whole rehabilitated building in service. Both dates fall in 2025, so the first credit year does not change, but the recapture period and the completion installment would start almost four months early.

citations.raw: DOC-15 p.10, update Jun 2025: "Architect issued the certificate of substantial completion on June 13"

cases.summary: Financial model puts the whole federal credit in 2025
cases.claims_compared: DOC-05 shows all federal credits delivered in tax year 2025 and none in 2026 to 2029. DOC-06 gives a July 15, 2025 placed-in-service date.

citations.quote: Federal credits delivered: 2025 5,120; 2026 to 2029 0 ($ in thousands)
citations.raw: DOC-05 p.4, 4.1: "Federal credits delivered: 2025 5,120; 2026 to 2029 0 ($ in thousands)"

cases.explanation: The credit is claimed in equal parts over five years. At $4,920,000, that is $984,000 a year for 2025 to 2029. Front-loading overstates the investor's early benefit and its return. The wrong credit amount is a separate case, HTC01-001.

cases.summary: Planned sale of a commercial unit falls inside the recapture period, but the memo says no transfers are planned
cases.claims_compared: DOC-15 plans to sell commercial unit C-1 by June 30, 2026. DOC-16 says no sale or transfer is planned during the credit period. DOC-11 bars selling any unit in the compliance period without investor consent.

citations.quote: We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026
citations.raw: DOC-15 p.12, update Oct 2025: "We plan to sell commercial unit C-1 to Danville Arts Collective, targeting June 30, 2026"

citations.quote: No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period
citations.raw: DOC-16 p.2, 7: "No sale or transfer of any part of the property is planned during the credit period"

citations.quote: No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent
citations.raw: DOC-11 p.24, Section 8.2: "No sale or transfer of the Building or any unit during the Compliance Period without Investor Member consent"

cases.explanation: A sale on June 30, 2026 falls in recapture year 1, which ends July 14, 2026, so credits already claimed on that unit's share of QRE would be recaptured in full. The memo leaves the plan out, and no investor consent is in the data room.
cases.alternative_readings: If the sale slips past July 14, 2026, recapture drops to 80%.
cases.open_questions: Has the investor consented, and what share of QRE belongs to unit C-1?

cases.summary: Equity bridge loan matures before the installment meant to repay it

citations.raw: DOC-04 p.1, line 9: "Equity bridge loan $1,700,000, matures 3/31/2026"
DOC-05 p.4, 4.3: "Installment 3 received June 30, 2026"
DOC-11 p.14, Section 4.2(c): "40% upon receipt of Part 3 approval"

cases.explanation: The loan falls due three months before its repayment source arrives, and that source depends on a Part 3 approval that is still pending. The bridge needs an extension or another source of cash.
cases.alternative_readings: The lender may already have agreed to extend the maturity.
cases.open_questions: Is there a bridge extension or a commitment to extend?

cases.summary: Model expects state credit proceeds after the buyer can walk away
cases.claims_compared: DOC-12 lets the buyer terminate if the DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026. DOC-05 expects Virginia credit proceeds on July 31, 2026.

citations.quote: If the DHR certification is not delivered by April 30, 2026, Buyer may terminate this Agreement

DOC-05 p.4, 4.4: "Virginia credit proceeds received July 31, 2026"

cases.explanation: DHR certification follows Part 3 approval. If the timing in the model holds, the buyer can terminate before closing and the deal loses $5,043,000 of expected proceeds.
cases.open_questions: Has the buyer agreed to extend the outside date?

citations.raw: DOC-16 p.2, 8: "credits remain subject to recapture through July 2030"

citations.raw: DOC-19 p.9: 'the QRE base is $36.45M going forward ... Some of the decks and exhibits still carry the $39.8M'

cases.summary: Operating agreement body was updated but its Exhibit B still carries the old credits
cases.claims_compared: Section 3.1(a) sets $6,269,400 as Projected Federal Credits times $0.86; Section 1.1 defines Projected Federal Credits by Exhibit B, which says $7,960,000.

citations.quote: equal to the product of (x) the Projected Federal Credits and (y) the Federal Credit Price, which amount the parties acknowledge equals ... ($6,269,400)
citations.raw: DOC-11 p.14, Section 3.1(a): 'equal to the product of (x) the Projected Federal Credits and (y) the Federal Credit Price, which amount the parties acknowledge equals ... ($6,269,400)'

citations.quote: Projected Federal Credits means ... twenty percent (20%) of the Projected QRE, as set forth on Exhibit B
citations.raw: DOC-11 p.6, Section 1.1: 'Projected Federal Credits means ... twenty percent (20%) of the Projected QRE, as set forth on Exhibit B'

citations.quote: Building C $2,750,000', 'Site and parking deck $600,000', 'Projected QRE (sum of (a) through (d)) $39,800,000
citations.raw: DOC-11 p.66, Exhibit B Schedule 1: 'Building C $2,750,000', 'Site and parking deck $600,000', 'Projected QRE (sum of (a) through (d)) $39,800,000'

cases.explanation: Read through its own definitions, Projected Federal Credits are 20% of the Schedule 1 total, which still includes Building C and the parking deck: 20% of $39,800,000 is $7,960,000, and $7,960,000 x 0.86 = $6,845,600, not the $6,269,400 the parties 'acknowledge'. The exhibit can only be changed by an amendment that refers to the definition, so the stale figure governs until amended.

citations.raw: DOC-11 p.34, Section 7.2: 'No management agreement shall provide for a management fee exceeding three and one-half percent (3.5%) of Gross Operating Revenues'

citations.quote: a monthly management fee equal to four percent (4%) of Gross Collections
citations.raw: DOC-22 p.9, Section 4.1: 'a monthly management fee equal to four percent (4%) of Gross Collections'

cases.explanation: The fee breaches the cap by half a percentage point of revenue, and the agreement was not approved under Section 7.2. It is also signed by the owner rather than the master tenant (see HTC02-020).
